# Papercuts — templartorrent

Small frictions hit while working, logged in the moment (D-027). None of these blocked anything; together they show where the project needs sanding down. Newest first.

- 2026-11-03 [claude] Running akr evidence add-many with records that lack observed_at printed two AKR-T022 errors and 'nothing written', then '3 evidence records written in one pass' on the next line although nothing was written; the success line should not print after a refused pass, and the help text could say add-many does not default observed_at to HEAD the way evidence add does.  `@templartorrent.papercut.running-akr-evidence-add-many-with-records-that/1`
- 2026-10-24 [claude] Running the workspace tests with TMPDIR on a real disk (to exercise storage on btrfs instead of tmpfs /tmp) fails ui::tests::paste_magnet_from_the_system_clipboard and window_close_saves_layout_and_resume with "path must be shorter than SUN_LEN": the activation listener's Unix socket lives under temp_dir(), so a TMPDIR under the repository is too long. Those two tests need a short socket directory independent of TMPDIR.  `@templartorrent.papercut.running-the-workspace-tests-with-tmpdir-on-a/1`
- 2026-10-24 [claude] Running the rbit fork's own `cargo test --lib` without features fails to compile ("cannot find type HttpTracker") because a test module still refers to it unconditionally after the fork made http-client optional; `--features http-client` builds and passes 160 tests. Running it in-tree also needs a copy outside vendor/rbit, or it writes a crate-local Cargo.lock that the fork notes say was removed.  `@templartorrent.papercut.running-the-rbit-fork-s-own-cargo-test-lib/1`
- 2026-10-22 [claude] Session::set_wanted only re-evaluated job completion when a piece verified or a recheck finished, so a restored job whose saved selection was applied after its recheck stayed Downloading with everything it wanted already on disk; the same stall affected a live job that deselects its last incomplete file. Fixed with resettle_completion in the engine and a regression test; anyone adding a new selection mutator must call it too.  `@templartorrent.papercut.session-set-wanted-only-re-evaluated-job/1`
- 2026-10-22 [claude] Resuming from the ledger, the inherited uncommitted tree failed `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` with three lints in templartorrent-storage and the adapter, although the latest evidence records said Clippy passed; the tree drifted after that evidence was recorded. Running the gates before trusting an evidence record for an uncommitted tree is the only defence until the tree is committed.  `@templartorrent.papercut.resuming-from-the-ledger-the-inherited/1`
- 2026-10-22 [claude] `knowledge.start` and `knowledge.search` with planning kinds returned nothing because the ledger held only two completed milestones and no live planning record for AGENTS.md step 4; the handoff state lived in a stale observation and in perf-results handoff.json files. Opened templartorrent.milestone.safety-and-peer-policy so the next session has a live key to pass to knowledge.context.  `@templartorrent.papercut.knowledge-start-and-knowledge-search-with/1`
- 2026-10-22 [claude] In integration/rbit-adapter/tests/driver.rs the `hold` fixture fault parks on `std::future::pending()` inside its request handler, so it stops reading after the first request and `stats.requests` never grows past one. A test waiting for four requests from a hold server hits its deadline. Added a `silent` fault that records requests and keeps reading for pipeline-depth assertions.  `@templartorrent.papercut.in-integration-rbit-adapter-tests-driver-rs-the/1`
- 2026-10-16 [grok] The production fixture scan include_str of lib.rs failed because the assertion literals contained the forbidden names. Build those needles at runtime so the test source is not a match.  `@templartorrent.papercut.the-production-fixture-scan-include-str-of-lib/1`
- 2026-10-15 [codex] While locating rbit's Info type I assumed metainfo/info.rs, which did not exist. rg --files and symbol search located the actual type and parser in src/metainfo/torrent.rs. Inventory before assuming a module layout.  `@templartorrent.papercut.while-locating-the-rbit-info-type-i-assumed/2`
- 2026-10-15 [codex] While locating audit scripts, rg reported no scripts directory; the repository stores reference checks in .github/workflows/reference.yml and uses cargo tree directly for the native-source dependency trace.  `@templartorrent.papercut.while-locating-audit-scripts-rg-reported-no/1`
- 2026-10-15 [codex] While inspecting rbit incoming handshakes I tried peer/handshake.rs; Handshake actually lives in peer/message.rs. Use rg to locate pinned upstream types before opening guessed paths.  `@templartorrent.papercut.while-inspecting-rbit-incoming-handshakes-i/1`
- 2026-10-15 [codex] The pinned rbit crate also uses peer.rs rather than peer/mod.rs. The registry module layout differs from common directory conventions; locate exported symbols with rg instead of assuming mod.rs paths.  `@templartorrent.papercut.the-pinned-rbit-crate-also-uses-peer-rs-rather/1`
- 2026-10-15 [codex] Orientation used positional akr context key; CLI requires --goal, unlike akr get. Retried with explicit --goal. Initial file inventory also referenced absent .agent scratch directory.  `@templartorrent.papercut.orientation-used-positional-akr-context-key-cli/1`
- 2026-10-15 [codex] Localhost rbit tests failed at TcpListener::bind with EPERM inside the workspace sandbox. The approved elevated cargo test rerun passed all 11 deterministic local tests; failures were socket policy, not torrent protocol.  `@templartorrent.papercut.localhost-rbit-tests-failed-at-tcplistener-bind/1`
- 2026-10-15 [codex] Localhost Driver tests compile in the sandbox but bind returns EPERM. Reran the same offline fixture command with escalation; no Internet endpoints are used.  `@templartorrent.papercut.localhost-driver-tests-compile-in-the-sandbox/1`
- 2026-10-15 [codex] Large apply_patch edits to the growing Driver missed exact contexts twice after formatting. Both were rejected atomically; split subsequent edits into smaller context-checked patches. Initial seeder fixtures also needed to accept the newly legitimate Bitfield/Have/Choke control messages.  `@templartorrent.papercut.large-apply-patch-edits-to-the-growing-driver/1`
- 2026-10-15 [codex] AKR strict validation flags observations watching new engine/storage directories because observed_at anchors HEAD before these untracked paths exist. Use a tracked parent glob until code is committed; dirty watched paths also emit the expected G004 freshness warning.  `@templartorrent.papercut.akr-strict-validation-flags-observations/1`
- 2026-10-15 [codex] AKR read/context accept revision-qualified references, but revise and complete require the bare key. Passing /3 or /1 was rejected; reran mutations with bare keys. Scratch prune ran after those errors, so recreated the status overlay from the preserved handoff artifact before retrying.  `@templartorrent.papercut.akr-read-context-accept-revision-qualified/1`
- 2026-10-15 [codex] A multi-file patch for allocation telemetry missed a context line after rustfmt changed the metric print layout. The patch was atomic; re-read the formatted lines and applied the changes in smaller patches.  `@templartorrent.papercut.a-multi-file-patch-for-allocation-telemetry/1`

## Not about this project

Frictions with something else — a tool, a harness — hit while working here. They are logged where they were hit; `akr papercut collate --about <subject>` is how the project that owns the subject gathers them.

- 2026-11-05 [claude] (claude-code) While porting to Windows, Rust text containing doubled backslashes (Windows paths, '\\' char literals) was silently collapsed when written through Bash heredocs and Python string literals: '\\' became '\' and '\t' became a tab, which broke compilation and put a tab in a doc comment. Write backslash-heavy Rust with the Edit/Write tools, not shell heredocs.  `@templartorrent.papercut.while-porting-to-windows-rust-text-containing/1`
- 2026-11-03 [grok] (git) git merge --no-commit refused to start, before showing conflicts, because this repo has no user.name or user.email. Exporting GIT_AUTHOR_* and GIT_COMMITTER_* for the command was enough.  `@templartorrent.papercut.git-merge-no-commit-refused-to-start-before/1`
- 2026-10-27 [grok] (cargo) cargo test --manifest-path vendor/rbit/Cargo.toml --lib fails to compile tracker tests because HttpTracker is behind the http-client feature, and it writes a gitignored vendor/rbit/Cargo.lock plus vendor/rbit/target. The workspace patch build does not do this. Run rbit's own suite with --features http-client from a copy, not against the vendored manifest.  `@templartorrent.papercut.cargo-test-manifest-path-vendor-rbit-cargo-toml/1`
- 2026-10-26 [claude] (akr) knowledge.revise accepted an observation whose observed_at named a commit that does not exist, and wrote the revision; only the next `akr check` reported AKR-G011. knowledge.propose rejects the same input up front. revise should run the same commit-presence check before writing.  `@templartorrent.papercut.knowledge-revise-accepted-an-observation-whose/1`
- 2026-10-22 [grok] (cargo) The peer-score acceptance command used cargo test --test with the test function name. Cargo treats --test as an integration-test target, so it exited 101 with no target named driver_corruption_retries_verified_piece_without_corrupting_files. The target is driver; the function name is a filter before --.  `@templartorrent.papercut.the-peer-score-acceptance-command-used-cargo/1`
- 2026-10-22 [grok] (git) Committing the resume bitmap failed with "Author identity unknown" because this repository has no local user.name or user.email, and the environment did not set them either. History is entirely dk <dkoepke@protonmail.com>. The commit went through by passing those as GIT_AUTHOR_* and GIT_COMMITTER_* for that command, without writing git config.  `@templartorrent.papercut.committing-the-resume-bitmap-failed-with-author/1`
- 2026-10-17 [grok] (x11) Capturing the TemplarTorrent window on DISPLAY=:1 failed the first script because import, scrot, and xwd are not installed (set -e exited before launch). ffmpeg x11grab of the xwininfo geometry worked. xdotool search --name TemplarTorrent also matches the pcmanfm desktop icon, so the window has to be found by pid.  `@templartorrent.papercut.capturing-the-templartorrent-window-on-display/1`
